item.title: An Arab Town in Israel Celebrates the Election but Wonders What Will Change
item.description: Gains for Arab-led parties have electrified Taibe, in central Israel, even as voters elsewhere in Israel say they have no place in any future government.
item.dc:creator: Adam Rasgon and Natan Odenheimer
item.media:description: Ahmad Tibi, a leader of the Joint List party, with supporters on Tuesday outside a polling station in Taibe, Israel, a predominantly Arab town. “We’re ready to swallow frogs to take down Netanyahu’s government,” he said.

item.title: Israel’s Election Is Unlikely to Change Its Policies and Global Isolation
item.description: The leading contenders, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot, aren’t substantially different in their approach to Israel’s security or in their opposition to a Palestinian state.
item.dc:creator: Steven Erlanger
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Campaign posters for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the Likud party, and Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, in Hadera, Israel, on Tuesday.

item.title: Police Investigate Former Prince Andrew and Epstein’s Time at Balmoral, Royal Estate in Scotland
item.description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor spent time with Jeffrey Epstein, the convicted sex offender, and his associate Ghislaine Maxwell, at Balmoral, the royal family’s Scottish retreat.

item.title: New ‘Call of Duty’ Game Draws Criticism for Using Footage of Deadly Seoul Crowd Crush

item.dc:creator: Max Kim
item.media:description: A “Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4” poster in Paris. The game is set in South Korea and depicts an invasion by its northern neighbor, against a backdrop of tensions between the United States and Russia.

item.title: Colombia’s ‘Narcoterrorist’ Crackdown Raises Questions Over Killings

item.media:credit: Federico Rios for The New York Times
item.media:description: Yuli Motta at her home in Guaviare province, Colombia. She says she witnessed the fatal shooting of Luis Carlos Mojica by members of the Colombian military last month.

item.title: Court Rejects Erin Patterson’s Appeal in Mushroom Murders Case

item.title: Rare Evacuation Announced by Melania Trump Begins in Ukrainian City of Oleshky

item.title: Another Toll of the Violent Unrest in France: The Political Center

item.dc:creator: Mark Landler
item.media:description: Édouard Philippe, the leading centrist candidate in France’s presidential race, has struggled in the polls since widespread protests broke out across the country last month.

item.title: How the Japanese Spy Drama ‘Vivant’ Became The Target of China’s Anger

item.title: Taking the Saga of a Criminal Gang From Page to Screen to Opera Stage

item.title: How a Self-Described ‘Junkie’ Rode Synthetic Drugs to Oblivion — and Fame

item.dc:creator: Azam Ahmed

item.media:description: The Estonian police used to respond to reports of people sniffing glue at these abandoned housing units. Now ultra-potent new synthetic drugs are keeping them busy.

item.title: Trump and His Aides Helped Bolsonaro Flee Brazil and Enter U.S.

item.title: How Ukrainian Soldiers Are Moving Underground
